name: /tutor-start
for: begin or continue the course
help: Starts the course: a short talk about you, a level, then one project. With a language (python, rust, go, typescript, lua, javascript) it starts in that language. `check` runs the small level task once you have done it, `off` pauses, `spec` writes the project plan again if it failed.

name: /tutor-help
for: open the help tab with every command
help: Opens a Neovim tab listing every command: what you type in the editor, what you type here in the tutor pane, and the keys for moving around. Press q in that tab to close it.

name: /tutor-level
for: set your level by hand
help: Sets your level from 0 (beginner) to 100 (pro). The tutor changes how much it helps. Without a number it shows your current level.

name: /tutor-status
for: show the tutor's current state
help: Shows what the tutor knows right now: level, language, project, and any open stuck episode.

name: /tutor-plan
for: walk a task from idea to code in six steps
help: The design recipe: takes a task from spec/tasks.md (for example P1.T1) through six steps, from understanding it to working code. Say "skip" to skip a step, `next` to move on, `off` to stop.

name: /tutor-done
for: check a task and tick it
help: Runs the task's checks and ticks it in spec/tasks.md when they pass. `anyway` ticks it without passing checks (it counts as unchecked).

name: /tutor-fix
for: pro only: show the fix for where you are stuck
help: At pro level, shows the fix for the spot you are stuck on. Other levels get it after a few tries.

name: /tutor-improve
for: make a ticked task's code better, measured
help: Takes a task you already ticked and works on making its code better, measured before and after. `done` finishes, `off` stops.

name: /tutor-notes
for: design and naming notes after a pro tick
help: Turns on or off the short notes on design and naming the tutor adds after you tick a task at pro level. They carry no points.

name: /tutor-lesson
for: learn-first lessons with small exercises
help: The learn-first path: short lessons on the ideas your project needs, each with a small exercise. `next` writes the exercise or starts the next round, `check` checks it, `skip` skips, `review` repeats, `off` stops.

name: /tutor-exam
for: a timed exam in this project
help: Starts a timed exam in this project, small or medium, optionally on a topic. `check` runs the exam's examples, `off` abandons it, `sandbox on|off` sets whether it runs in a sandbox.

name: /tutor-submit
for: hand in the exam and get it graded
help: Hands in the running exam: runs its tests, grades it and writes exam/<id>/grade.md.

name: /tutor-step-up
for: step up to the next band
help: The step-up to the next band: a talking test, then a coding test. `check` runs the coding test's checks, `submit` hands it in.

name: /tutor-architect
for: talk architecture: parts, data flow, trade-offs
help: Switches the tutor to an architecture professor: components, how data flows, trade-offs, with diagrams and no code. `off` returns to the coding tutor.

name: /tutor-progress
for: your habits, hint use, exams and concepts
help: Shows your progress: habits with their latest evidence, how much help you used over time, exams, and a concept map.

name: /tutor-memory
for: what the tutor remembers about you
help: Lists what the tutor remembers about you. Pick one to make it forget.

name: /tutor-feedback
for: tell the tutor how it is teaching
help: Tells the tutor how its teaching lands: too-long, too-vague, too-much-help or good. It adjusts from then on.

name: /tutor-thinking
for: show or hide the model's thinking
help: Shows or hides the model's thinking in the pane: auto (hidden), show, hide.

name: /tutor-learn
for: keep what you learned from being stuck
help: Drafts a skill from the last stuck episode you finished. Edit it, then submit to keep it or press Esc to discard.

name: /tutor-docs
for: fetch official docs for a language
help: Fetches (or fetches again) the official docs for a language, so the tutor can quote them.

name: /tutor-checker
for: a second model checks each reply
help: Sets a second model that reads each held reply against the turn's rule before you see it. `off` turns it off.

name: /reload
for: reload the tutor extension
help: Pi's own command: reloads extensions, skills and prompts, for example after an update.

name: :Tutor
for: open or close the tutor pane
help: Opens the tutor pane on the right, or hides it again. The tutor keeps running while hidden.

name: :TutorRestart
for: restart the tutor in its pane
help: Stops the tutor in the pane and starts it again. Your course and project are kept.

name: :TutorRun
for: run your program in a split below
help: Runs your program in a split below the editor: you see its output and type its input there. `test` runs the project's tests instead, `stop` stops a run. Press q in the split to close it.

name: :TutorTour
for: the tour: Neovim and the tutor, step by step
help: A short guided tour: the Neovim basics you need, then how to use the tutor (the pane, running code, asking for help). It remembers where you stopped. `restart` starts over, `off` stops.

name: <leader>te
for: ask the tutor about the error under the cursor
help: In the editor, on a line with an error: sends the error, the line and its code to the tutor as your question. Right-click on the line and pick "Ask tutor about this error" does the same.

name: <Esc><Esc>
for: leave the tutor pane's typing mode
help: Inside the tutor pane you are in terminal mode: keys go to the tutor. Press Esc twice to get Neovim's normal mode back, then <C-w>h to go to your code.

name: <C-w>h
for: move to the window on the left (your code)
help: Ctrl-w then h moves to the window on the left; <C-w>l moves right (to the tutor pane). Use it after <Esc><Esc> to get back to your code.

name: q
for: close the run split (after the program ends)
help: In the run split below the editor, once the program has ended, q closes the split.
